title: Benjamin Franklin — Catching Lightning With a Kite, Leyden Jar & Copper Lightning Rod (1752)

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In 1752, one wild man flew a kite into a storm—to catch lightning on a key!

lines.speaker: william
lines.text: Father, stop—that lightning bolt could kill us!

lines.speaker: franklin
lines.text: Touch the brass key, William—lightning is pure electricity!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He bottled real storm lightning in a glass Leyden jar—naming positive and negative charge!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then Franklin built the copper lightning rod—

lines.speaker: william
lines.text: Whoa! It steered a thunderbolt straight into the earth!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One fearless storm test saved millions of homes, and sparked the entire electric age!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Skyscrapers, batteries, your phone right now—all trace back to Benjamin Franklin!
